# `silk/collections/id`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Typed 32-bit row numbers.

## When to use
Use [`Id`](#Id) for a row number that code stores: a link from one row to another row, or a key that
names a row of one collection. An `Id<Fragment>` is a different type from an `Id<Box>`, so the
compiler rejects a row number that is used with rows of the wrong type. An `Id` is 4 bytes, half
of a `usize` on a 64-bit target. Use a plain `usize` for a loop counter.

## Details
An [`Id`](#Id) holds one `u32`. [`Id.none`](#Id.impl.none) is the value that names no row. It replaces a sentinel
such as `usize.MAX`. `silk.collections.column_list.ColumnList` accepts an `Id<T>` as the index
of its `T` rows, as in `fragments[id].size`.

## Gotchas
An `Id` is not checked when it is made. A row index traps when its `Id` names no row.

## Examples
### Follow a link from one row to the next row
```silk
import silk.collections.column_list { ColumnList }
import silk.collections.id { Id }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.ownership { Copy }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }

struct Step {
  pub next: Id<Step>,
  pub cost: u32,
}

impl Copy for Step {}

effect fn total() -> u32
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut steps = ColumnList<Step>.make()
  let last = run steps.appendId(Step { next: Id<Step>.none(), cost: 5 })
  let first = run steps.appendId(Step { next: last, cost: 2 })
  let mut sum: u32 = 0
  let mut current = first
  while !current.isNone() {
    sum = sum + steps[current].cost
    current = steps[current].next
  }
  return sum
}

effect fn recover(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> u32 {
  return 0
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let sum = run total()
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
    |> Effect.catchAll(recover)
  if sum != 7 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `Id`

```silk
pub struct Id<T>
```

The number of a row of `T`, in 32 bits.

### Details

The type parameter only names the rows that the number belongs to. An `Id<T>` is `Copy`, and two
of them compare by their numbers. [`Id.none`](#Id.impl.none) names no row.

<a id="Id.impl.fromIndex"></a>

### Associated function `fromIndex`

```silk
pub fn fromIndex(index: usize) -> Id<T>
```

Returns the id of the row at `index`.

#### Gotchas

It traps if `index` is 4,294,967,295 or more, because that number is [`Id.none`](#Id.impl.none) and larger
numbers do not fit in 32 bits.

<a id="Id.impl.fromRaw"></a>

### Associated function `fromRaw`

```silk
pub fn fromRaw(value: u32) -> Id<T>
```

Returns the id that has the number `value`. The number 4,294,967,295 gives [`Id.none`](#Id.impl.none).

<a id="Id.impl.none"></a>

### Associated function `none`

```silk
pub fn none() -> Id<T>
```

Returns the id that names no row.

#### When to use

Use it as the value of a link that has no target, such as the next sibling of the last
child. Test for it with [`Id.isNone`](#Id.impl.isNone).

<a id="Id.impl.isNone"></a>

### Method `isNone`

```silk
pub fn isNone(self: Self) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if the id is [`Id.none`](#Id.impl.none).

<a id="Id.impl.index"></a>

### Method `index`

```silk
pub fn index(self: Self) -> usize
```

Returns the row index that the id names.

#### Gotchas

[`Id.none`](#Id.impl.none) gives 4,294,967,295, which is not the index of a row.

<a id="Id.impl.raw"></a>

### Method `raw`

```silk
pub fn raw(self: Self) -> u32
```

Returns the number that the id holds. [`Id.none`](#Id.impl.none) gives 4,294,967,295.
